newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Suspected Arab collaborator found dead near Nablus.
newsitem.headline: Suspected Arab collaborator found dead near Nablus.

text.p: Israeli troops on Saturday discovered the body of a Palestinian who had been shot in the head and who was suspected of collaborating with Israel, officials said.

"The body of a Palestinian who holds an Israeli identification card -- the kind Israel gives to collaborators to protect them -- was found east of Nablus in an area outside the security control of the Palestinian Authority," said Nablus governor Mahmoud al-Aloul.
An Israeli police spokesman said soldiers discovered the body while on patrol near the West Bank city. He said the man had been tortured and shot in the head.
"The body was taken to the forensics institute for an autopsy," the spokesman said.
In Nablus, a Palestinian court charged four Palestinians with collaborating with Israel and other offences, witnesses said.
Three of the four defendants were members of a branch of Palestinian security. One suspect admitted in court kidnapping Palestinians wanted by Israel, witnesses said.
Palestinians have killed scores of fellow-Arabs suspected of collaborating with Israel and many have been detained by PLO police.
Israeli authorities have allowed many collaborators to take up residence in Israel since it transferred control of parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip to the PLO in 1994.
